lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Bloomberg Terminal
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Move Experience above Education.
items.because: Employers will usually want to see your several years of relevant work first.

items.says: Give the caddie role less space than the finance roles.
items.because: It explains your current employment, but its relevance to finance is limited.

items.says: Make dates, currencies, and number formatting consistent, and avoid hard-to-scan bullet breaks.
items.because: Consistent formatting makes the résumé easier to scan.

items.says: Consider a target-role headline or short summary if it would focus the application.
items.because: It should be tailored to the roles you’re applying for rather than repeat the skills list.

items.says: Consider adding a major focus, GPA, or relevant coursework if it strengthens your candidacy.
items.because: Those details are most useful when your academic record is strong or education is especially relevant to the role.

items.says: Use the same location and date format as the rest of the résumé.
items.because: It would make the document more consistent and easier to scan.

items.says: Clarify whether about five rounds a week is typical year-round or seasonal.
items.because: Seasonality may affect how readers interpret the figure.

items.says: Show more of your contribution rather than only your workload.
items.because: The current wording offers little to help a finance employer assess your contribution.

items.says: Specify your role or scope in the junior tournament.
items.because: “Helped” does not show what you were responsible for.

items.says: Define “close efficiency” and give the measure’s baseline and result.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether the 40% improvement concerns close duration, manual effort, or something else.

items.says: Include the tools or process changes if relevant.
Clarify whether the template was adopted across all 12 requests and what effect it had.
items.because: The stated result shows common rules, but an operational or business effect would make it stronger.

items.says: Explain the 5% threshold, your ownership of the commentary, and whether it informed decisions.
items.because: It is unclear whether you covered every qualifying variance or only selected items.

items.says: The FCFE valuation uses WACC rather than the discount rate normally used for FCFE.
items.because: FCFE normally calls for the cost of equity; WACC is normally used with free cash flow to the firm.

items.says: Clarify the valuation conclusion or how the analysis was used.
Adding three business-unit EBITDA margins does not produce a group EBITDA margin.
items.because: A consolidated margin uses total EBITDA divided by total revenue.

items.says: Explain how forecast error was measured and over what period.
items.because: That context would make the accuracy claim clearer.

items.says: Specify the observation period and, if available, the performance window for the full approved group.
items.because: Readers need enough context to judge the zero-default sample and timeframe.

items.says: Clarify the period covered and what “early defaults” means.
Avoid implying the threshold changes alone caused the approval increase unless you can support it.
items.because: The before-and-after rates do not by themselves establish that attribution.

items.says: “Writes” uses the wrong tense for this role.
items.because: The role ended in December 2022.

items.says: Clarify whether you created, maintained, or introduced the checklist and when missed tests fell.
Specify which credit memos the time reduction covers.
items.because: “Each credit memo” could refer to a particular memo type or typical workflow.

items.says: Name the tools or process involved if useful.
items.because: That could add context to the measured time reduction.

items.says: Give the valuation date or explain the comparison behind “within 6% of the market price.”
items.because: Proximity to market price alone does not establish that a valuation was accurate.

items.says: Name the company or ticker if appropriate to disclose.
Specify whether the discount-rate change is one percentage point.
items.because: “A 1-point change” is unclear.

items.says: State the assumptions behind both share values and check them against the model.
Clarify whether the club used the analysis in its pitch or only considered it.
items.because: The current wording implies adoption; if it was used, its role in the pitch is also unclear.

items.says: Check whether “FP&A team” accurately describes the student-fund work and clarify the organization.
items.because: FP&A sounds like a corporate finance function that may not fit a student investment fund.

items.says: Explain what you changed in the report or how it improved committee analysis.
items.because: The bullet shows adoption but gives little detail about the work itself.

items.says: The cash-forecast claim appears to duplicate the Stonebridge forecast.
items.because: The scale, accuracy, timeframe, and debt outcome match, raising accuracy concerns and making the experience look padded.

items.says: Add relevant tools used in your analyst work, if you can discuss them.
items.because: ERP, reporting, or data tools may be relevant to target roles.

items.says: Make the Methods list more specific where your experience supports it.
items.because: The current list is relevant but broad.
